deploybot: [SEC-GATE] release/rc9 blocked: SBOM mismatch + vuln scan found CVE-2026-31415 in transitive dep 'img-lite' (medium, patch available). staging canary quarantined :warning:
Maria: ugh, thanks @deploybot. Is this in the runtime path or just a dev tool?
James: looks transitive via 'pdf-renderer' -> 'img-lite'. Not used in main inference path but pulled into the utility container we ship with batch jobs.
Sara: does the SBOM show an unexpected upstream source or a digest mismatch?
deploybot: SBOM diff snippet:
```
- img-lite@1.2.3 (sha256:aaa...)
+ img-lite@1.2.3 (sha256:bbb...)  <-- provenance mismatch
```
Kevin: that digest change is suspicious. Could be benign rebuild, but vuln scan flags the CVE present in the artifact with digest bbb.
Olivia: security here. CVE-2026-31415 affects image parsing in certain paths. Impact to inference likely low, but we need documented risk acceptance or remove from release. Legal/compliance want SBOM provenance resolved for GA.
Anil: CI shows canary uptake 3 hosts, all quarantined by the gate. Canary change window is until 10:00 UTC. We can either pin to the older digest (if available), rollback to rc8, or request an exception with mitigation.
Maria: we don't have a patched version in upstream yet? deploybot mentioned patch available — where is it?
deploybot: package registry has img-lite@1.2.4 with patch. But our internal image build uses lockfiles pinned to sha256:bbb, and the new build requires rebuilding images and rerunning SBOM proving.
James: rebuild + re-SBOM could be a quick follow if we can automate: rebuild utility container, run sbom-prove, run vuln scan. Estimate ~45m in best case.
Sara: alternative: pin the component in the release manifest to img-lite@1.2.2 (known-good digest) to unblock, then follow up with a rebuild and new SBOM. Pinning is less risky than rollback for product changes.
Olivia: compliance preference is to have a provenance trace; pinning to an older digest is acceptable if we document why and schedule remediation. We need a ticket and approval from security lead.
Kevin: action options:
- A) Pin to known-good digest and proceed with canary after doc + security signoff.
- B) Full rollback to rc8 (safer but loses other fixes).
- C) Hold the release and do rebuild+re-SBOM (slower).
Maria: I prefer A for speed, unless legal objects. Can we auto-generate the SBOM proof after pin?
Anil: yes, CI can run sbom-prove on pin change. I can trigger the job if we decide now.
Olivia: I can approve a documented pin if the temporary mitigation is: 1) pin to 1.2.2, 2) create security ticket SEC-2237 with owner, 3) schedule rebuild+re-SBOM and deploy within a 24h timebox, 4) revert pin once proven.
James: agree. We should also add a canary rule to limit traffic to 5% until rebuild lands.
Sara: deploy command to pin:
```bash
ci-edit-manifest --component utility-container --set img-lite=1.2.2 --commit "pin img-lite to avoid CVE-2026-31415"
```
Maria: if we do pin+canary, can we add an automated rollback trigger if the canary shows errors?
Anil: yes, can set canary-failure-threshold to 3 errors/host and deploybot will rollback automatically.
Olivia: I'll add the approval comment in SEC-2237: "Security approves pin-and-timebox remediation; must complete full rebuild+provenance within 24h or rollback."
Kevin: timeline decision: if CI job finishes and SBOM proof is generated by 09:30 UTC, we allow canary expansion to 5%. If not, we roll back to rc8 at the 10:00 UTC change window.
Maria: I'll open the PR now and trigger CI. tagging @Olivia @Anil for follow-up.
James: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-manifests/pull/492 :eyes:
Anil: CI triggered, sbom-prove job started.
deploybot: Canary quarantine cleared for host-3 after pin PR merged (provisional).
Olivia: noted in SEC-2237, assigning to Maria.
Sara: thanks all. agreeing to pin+timebox. I'll add a release note blurb under "known issues": "Utility container pinned to img-lite@1.2.2 due to transient CVE detection; rebuild and provenance pending." :memo:
Kevin: I'll watch canary metrics and will rollback if errors > threshold. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks. closing thread once rebuild proof is in.
